correctness.rationale: Complementarity of two-phase firing vectors follows from the connected-graph Laplacian; independent threshold intervals give the exact cut-degree weight. Two binomial local-CLT factors yield the sharp \(\sqrt{\pi n}/4\) constant; an endpoint maximal-binomial bound establishes tightness. Each deleted edge contributes exactly \(2/n\) to the logarithmic correction and bounded-degree hypergeometric variances force concentration, uniformly for all allowed missing-edge patterns. The degree-product logarithm completes the equivalence. Direct state-level finite checks and independently computed combinatorial formulas agree; finite experiments are corroboration only.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The proof isolates the incremental nontrivial assertion: conditional on the firing counts, deleted-edge correction has expectation exactly \(2m/n\) and vanishing variance uniformly in all bounded-degree deletion patterns. That establishes a genuinely stronger family asymptotic than any of the cited baseline statements.

They are equivalent in the fixed-degree regime via the degree-product logarithm. Graph switching, relabelling, and the deletion of a perfect matching are included but do not exhaust the arbitrary irregular family.

value.rationale: The theorem characterizes a natural, nontrivial graph-perturbation universality class for an infinite family of discrete dynamical systems. Arbitrary sparse but adversarial edge defects destroy complete-biclique symmetry, yet both the sharp orbit-count normalization and a nonuniform beta/arcsine firing law persist with an exact exponential defect correction. This is a structural stability theorem, not a table lookup or a single parameter extension.
